concepts.name: The call of the prophet
concepts.why: All readers (does the text say this?): the name 'I am sending you' is said by Exod 3:10, Ezek 2:3 and Jer 1:7 only. 1 Sam 3:10 (Samuel answering) and Jer 1:5 (set apart, appointed) say no sending, and Amos 7:15 says 'Go, prophesy'. Either rename to a plain label such as 'The call of the prophet' (Isa 6:8 still carries its note) or drop 1 Sam 3:10 and Jer 1:5.

Secular scholar / all readers: the name is 'The throne of David', but Amos 9:11 says 'the fallen tent of David' and Jer 23:5 says a Branch raised up for David who will reign as King; neither names a throne. The drafter kept Amos 9:11 because it names David, but the name promises a throne. The other six (2 Sam 7:16, Ps 132:11, Isa 9:7, Jer 33:17, Luke 1:32, Acts 2:30) all say throne. Drop the two, or rename the concept to something both fit, such as 'I will raise up for David'. The side-by-side with Luke 1:32 and Acts 2:30 is acceptable as it stands: each speaks in its own words and nothing says one fulfils another.

Secular scholar / Jewish reader: the name says 'spoken through the prophet', but John 19:24 says 'the Scripture' and quotes a psalm, not a prophet. The other seven all say prophet or Isaiah/Jeremiah. Drop John 19:24, or widen the name to the bare formula 'To fulfill what was spoken'. The concept is otherwise sound for the fulfilment question: every passage is a New Testament verse that says the formula itself, each is quoted, and none is a site statement that an OT passage points to a NT one.

All readers: the name is Luke 24:27 and the concept is what the NT says of the prophets as a whole. Luke 4:21 ('Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing') names neither Moses nor the Prophets in the verse itself; the Isaiah scroll lies in the previous verses. Drop it, or add Luke 4:17-20 if it is wanted. The rest (Matt 5:17, Luke 24:27, 24:44, Acts 3:24, 10:43, Rom 1:2, 1 Pet 1:10) say it in the New Testament's own words and are fairly framed as such.

concepts.name: The Spirit and prophesying
concepts.why: Baptist / Pentecostal / Reformed / secular reader: 'I will pour out My Spirit on all people' is Joel 2:28 and Acts 2:18, but Num 11:25 (seventy elders), 1 Sam 10:10 (Saul), Ezek 2:2 (Ezekiel) and Acts 21:9 (Philip's daughters) are the Spirit on some, so the name says more than most of its passages, and it leans toward one view of Acts 2. A plain label fits all eight and keeps Joel and Acts 2:16, 18 in their own words.

Reformed / dispensational / Jewish reader: the name is 'I will make a new covenant', but Ezek 36:26 says a new heart and spirit and the word covenant does not appear. Reading it as the new covenant is the tradition's link, and Christians and Jewish readers divide on it. Jer 31:31, 31:33, 32:40, Ezek 37:26 and Heb 8:8 all say covenant. Drop Ezek 36:26 (it fits the Spirit concept or the hope concept).

secondary_or_links: Drop the link 'Kingdom'. The theme's only Davidic-throne material is concept 26, which the Messiah/Christology and Covenant links already cover, whereas each of the other ten has a concept of its own (Sacrifice 14; Apocalyptic 6, 8, 9, 33; Church 31; Spirit 30).
Secondaries: no change. All nine cite single verses and are plain labels.
